extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, institutional administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how recipients must respond to sexual harassment as sex discrimination under Title IX, including definitions, grievance procedures, supportive measures, due process, and limits on remedies and enforcement. Intended to inform institutional policy, procedures, and legal analysis of compliance and challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaliation (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department has included a provision in §106.71 to prohibit retaliation for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX or these final regulations or because the individual has made a report or complaint, testified, assisted, participated, or refused to participate in any manner in an investigation, proceeding, or hearing under these final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained as a required protection; discussed in more detail in the 'Retaliation' subsection of the 'Miscellaneous' preamble section. Recipients must ensure policies and procedures bar retaliation against anyone for participating in the Title IX process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures promptly (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer supportive measures to a complainant in response to a report of sexual harassment in the recipient's education program or activity against a person in the United States, irrespective of whether a complainant files a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to §106.44(a), the Title IX Coordinator must promptly contact the complainant to discuss the availability of supportive measures as defined in §106.30, consider the complainant's wishes, inform the complainant of availability with or without filing a formal complaint, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint. The Department views offering such measures as part of fulfilling obligations beyond the Supreme Court's deliberate indifference framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'complainant' (§106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department defines a complainant as 'an individual who is alleged to be the victim of conduct that could constitute sexual harassment' under §106.30 and uses the word 'victim' in that context; it removed the phrase 'or on whose behalf the Title IX Coordinator has filed a formal complaint.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: 'complainant' better aligns with Title IX obligations to respond to reports whether or not a formal complaint is filed. Recipients should use this definition when implementing policies and when Title IX Coordinators act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to respond to reports irrespective of formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Under these final regulations, a recipient has an obligation to respond to a report of sexual harassment that occurs in its education program or activity against a person in the United States, irrespective of whether the complainant chooses to file a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation includes offering supportive measures promptly and informing complainants of the process for filing a formal complaint. It clarifies that Title IX duties attach to reports, not only to formal complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process adapted to sexual harassment (§106.45) and due process role
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance process in §106.45 is designed to assess allegations of sexual harassment as a form of sex discrimination and provides procedural protections consistent with constitutional due process; it does not demand a particular outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department interprets due process as a flexible concept tailored to particular situations; the grievance process differs for elementary/secondary schools and postsecondary institutions. Recipients retain significant discretion within §106.45, may adopt reasonable rules of decorum applied equally, and the process is not intended to second-guess administrators' disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation obligation when complainant files formal complaint (§106.44(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(b)(1), a recipient is obligated to investigate allegations in a formal complaint if the complainant exercises the option of filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigating a filed formal complaint triggers the grievance procedures; recipients that comply with §106.44 (offering supportive measures and explaining process) will be better positioned to defend against claims of deliberate indifference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Supreme Court deliberate indifference rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations align Title IX administrative enforcement more closely with the rubric the Supreme Court adopted in Title IX cases (notably Davis) while mandating that recipients support alleged victims beyond that framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department adopted/adapted the deliberate indifference standard to retain flexibility for school disciplinary decisions and avoid courts second-guessing administrators. Regulations are intended to provide clarity to recipients and may decrease litigation by setting standards consistent with Court precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must respect First Amendment protections (§106.6(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations expressly state in §106.6(d)(1) that nothing in Title IX implementing regulations requires a recipient to restrict any rights that would otherwise be protected from government action by the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients remain free to determine admissions and other expressive decisions within constitutional bounds; grievance procedures must be implemented consistent with First Amendment limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility of due process across educational levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department acknowledges that different procedural due process protections may be required in different situations and does not mandate the same grievance process for elementary and secondary schools as for postsecondary institutions because due process is a 'flexible' concept dictated by a particular situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should tailor procedures to the institutional context while meeting the regulatory baseline; the final regulations are 'adapted for a particular situation' of addressing sexual harassment as sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to regulate sexual harassment under Title IX (delegation/intelligible principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress conferred authority on the Department to implement Title IX (20 U.S.C. 1682); statutory text and Supreme Court precedent support the Department's authority to regulate sexual harassment as sex discrimination and to prescribe grievance procedures consistent with constitutional due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department's rulemaking is justified by statute and precedent; the preamble explains the intelligible principle doctrine and rejects claims that the agency lacks delegated authority. Recipients should treat these regulations as within the Department's delegated power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spending Clause constraints on federal conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions attached to federal funding must satisfy Spending Clause limits: Congress must speak unambiguously, conditions must relate to the federal interest in particular national projects or programs, they must advance the general welfare, and they must not be coercive such that pressure turns into compulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department concludes the final regulations comport with Spending Clause limitations (provide notice, relate to Title IX's purposes, are not coercive, and further general welfare). Recipients may rely on the preamble's analysis when assessing constitutional challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and enforcement (§106.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised §106.3(a) to remove reference to monetary damages as a potential remedy that the Department may seek when administratively enforcing Title IX and its implementing regulations, referring instead to the Department's authority to enforce Title IX pursuant to 20 U.S.C. 1682.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative enforcement remedies are thus limited as reflected in §106.3(a); this affects the practical incentives for complainants choosing administrative versus court remedies and is part of the Department's assessment of litigation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact and effect on small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) addresses the costs of compliance, including on small entities; the Department does not believe these final regulations would place a substantial burden on small entities, including small elementary and secondary schools and small postsecondary institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consult the RIA for estimated compliance costs. The Department believes benefits outweigh compliance costs and that protections (supportive measures, due process) should not vary based on institution size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential litigation risk and how compliance mitigates it
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters argued the rules could increase litigation; the Department disagrees and believes these final regulations may decrease litigation by providing clarity and standardized grievance processes consistent with due process and Supreme Court precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical example: a recipient that promptly offers supportive measures and follows §106.44(a) and §106.45 may better defend against deliberate indifference claims and procedural due process claims by showing compliance with regulatory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing conflicts with Title VII and state/local laws (§106.6(f), §106.6(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department disagrees that these final regulations conflict with obligations under Title VII or with State, local, or tribal laws or rules, and addresses possible conflicts in the 'Section 106.6(f) Title VII and Directed Question 3 (Application to Employees)' and 'Section 106.6(h) Preemptive Effect' subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should review those specific subsections for how to reconcile obligations; the Department asserts no direct conflict and provides guidance on preemption and interplay with Title VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date should allow implementation and avoid mid-school-year disruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters requested an effective date to allow recipients to implement policy changes, training, procedures, etc., and asked that the final regulations not take effect in the middle of a school year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department acknowledges the concern; institutions should plan implementation timelines that allow training and policy updates. (Preamble records commenters' input though changes section for this chunk indicates comments received; consult final 'Effective Date' section for the Department's decision.)
